# Libraries

```{r libraries}
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

library(ggrepel)
library(Rtsne)
library(knitr)
```




# Introduction

This exploratory study investigates the mechanisms of apoptosis in HIV-infected cell lines. 
We applied PCA and t-SNE to RNA-seq data (Jurkat and J-Lat2 cells treated with DMSO, SAHA, 
or PMA across three replicates) as an initial quality control and dimension reduction step 
prior to differential expression analysis. Since the samples were processed in 
three distinct batches, we will also evaluate the presence of batch effects

**Experimental design:**
```{r experimental_design}
# Overview of the experimental design
design_summary <- data.frame(
  Factor = c("Cell line", "Treatment", "Replicates"),
  Levels = c("Jurkat T cells (HIV-negative), J-Lat2 (latent HIV infection)",
             "DMSO (control), SAHA (HDAC inhibitor), PMA",
             "3 independent experiments (rep1, rep2, rep3)")
)
kable(design_summary, caption = "Table 1: Summary of the Experimental Design")
```
The dataset was provided as a raw counts matrix (genes x samples) and an
associated sample sheet. Batch effects may be present across replicates and
normalization will be performed accordingly.





# Question 1 – Load, Adapt the Data and Create Metadata

## 1.1 Load the counts matrix

The counts file stores genes as rows and samples as columns.  
The sample sheet uses `;` as delimiter and contains three metadata variables:
`cell_type`, `treatment`, and `replicate`.

```{r load_data}
counts_raw <- read.csv("data/counts.csv", row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE)

sample_sheet <- read.csv("data/sample_sheet.csv", sep = ";", row.names = 1)

cat("Counts matrix dimensions (genes × samples):", dim(counts_raw), "\n")
cat("Sample sheet dimensions:", dim(sample_sheet), "\n")
```

## 1.2 Verify dimensions and sample order

We check that every column name in the counts matrix appears exactly once in the
sample sheet rows, and that their order matches.

```{r verify_order}
all_present <- all(colnames(counts_raw) %in% rownames(sample_sheet))
cat("All count columns present in sample sheet:", all_present, "\n")

sample_sheet <- sample_sheet[colnames(counts_raw), ]

order_ok <- all(colnames(counts_raw) == rownames(sample_sheet))
cat("Sample order matches between counts and metadata:", order_ok, "\n")
```

## 1.3 Adapt the data – transpose to samples × genes

PCA and t-SNE expect rows = samples, columns = variables (genes).

```{r transpose}
counts_t <- as.data.frame(t(counts_raw))   # samples × genes

cat("Transposed matrix dimensions (samples × genes):", dim(counts_t), "\n")
```

## 1.4 Metadata dataframe

```{r metadata}
metadata <- sample_sheet

metadata$group <- paste(metadata$cell_type, metadata$treatment, sep = "_")

kable(head(metadata, 10), caption = "First 10 rows of the metadata dataframe")
```

```{r metadata_summary}
design_tbl <- metadata %>%
  group_by(cell_type, treatment, replicate) %>%
  summarise(n_samples = n(), .groups = "drop")

kable(design_tbl, caption = "Experimental design: number of samples per group")
```


Interpretation:
The experimental design is slightly unbalanced across conditions, as the number of samples
varies across replicates.The replicate variable indicates the experimental batch, 
which we will use to track potential batch effects in PCA and t-SNE



# Question 2 – PCA Representation

## 2.1 Helper function for PCA plotting

We define a reusable function to avoid code duplication.

```{r pca_function}
run_pca <- function(mat, scale. = FALSE, center = TRUE) {
  prcomp(mat, scale. = scale., center = center)
}

pca_var_explained <- function(pca_obj) {
  var_exp <- pca_obj$sdev^2 / sum(pca_obj$sdev^2) * 100
  data.frame(
    PC       = seq_along(var_exp),
    variance = var_exp
  )
}

pca_scores_df <- function(pca_obj, metadata, pc1 = 1, pc2 = 2) {
  df <- as.data.frame(pca_obj$x[, c(pc1, pc2)])
  colnames(df) <- c("PC1", "PC2")
  cbind(df, metadata)
}

plot_scree <- function(var_df, n = 15, title = "Scree plot") {
  ggplot(var_df[1:n, ], aes(x = PC, y = variance)) +
    geom_col(fill = "lightblue2", colour = "white") +
    geom_line(colour = "darkred", size = 0.8) +
    geom_point(colour = "darkred", size = 2) +
    labs(title = title,
         x = "Principal Component", y = "Variance explained (%)") +
    theme_bw(base_size = 12)
}

plot_pca <- function(scores_df, colour_var, shape_var = NULL,
                     title = "PCA", xlab = "PC1", ylab = "PC2",
                     palette = NULL) {
  p <- ggplot(scores_df, aes_string(x = "PC1", y = "PC2",
                                    colour = colour_var,
                                    shape  = shape_var)) +
    geom_point(size = 3, alpha = 0.85) +
    labs(title = title, x = xlab, y = ylab) +
    theme_bw(base_size = 12) +  
    theme(legend.position = "right")
  if (!is.null(palette)) p <- p + scale_colour_manual(values = palette)
  p
}
```

## 2.2 Raw (non-scaled, non-normalised) PCA

```{r pca_raw}
pca_raw <- run_pca(counts_t, scale. = FALSE, center = TRUE)

var_raw  <- pca_var_explained(pca_raw)
sc_raw   <- pca_scores_df(pca_raw, metadata)

xlab_raw <- paste0("PC1 (", round(var_raw$variance[1], 1), "%)")
ylab_raw <- paste0("PC2 (", round(var_raw$variance[2], 1), "%)")

p1 <- plot_scree(var_raw, title = "Scree plot – Raw counts")

p2 <- plot_pca(sc_raw, colour_var = "cell_type", shape_var = "treatment",
               title = "PCA – Raw counts (colour = cell type)",
               xlab = xlab_raw, ylab = ylab_raw)

p3 <- plot_pca(sc_raw, colour_var = "replicate", shape_var = "treatment",
               title = "PCA – Raw counts (colour = replicate / batch)",
               xlab = xlab_raw, ylab = ylab_raw)
#CUANDO HAGA KNIT A VER COMO QUEDA ESTO. (BORRAR COMENTARIO PARA ENTREGAR CODIGO)
grid.arrange(p1, p2, p3, ncol = 2)
```

**Interpretation – Raw PCA:** As expected, the PCA on raw counts is heavily dominated by differences in library size rather than biological signal, with highly expressed genes distorting the projection. Grouping by replicate already reveals a noticeable batch effect, as samples from the same condition but different batches separate along PC2.

As expected, the PCA on raw counts is heavily dominated by differences in library size 
rather than biological signal, with highly expressed genes distorting the projection. 
Grouping by replicate already reveals a noticeable 
batch effect, as samples from the same condition but different batches separate along PC2.

## 2.3 Log-normalisation (CPM + log2)

To reduce library-size bias we compute **log2(CPM + 1)**.

```{r normalise}
library_sizes <- rowSums(counts_t) 


counts_cpm <- sweep(counts_t, MARGIN = 1, STATS = library_sizes, FUN = "/") * 1000000

counts_log <- log2(counts_cpm + 1)

cat("Library sizes – summary:\n"); print(summary(library_sizes))

```

```{r boxplot_normalisation, fig.height=5}
set.seed(42)
idx <- sample(nrow(counts_t), 20)
labels_sub <- paste(metadata$cell_type[idx], metadata$treatment[idx],
                    metadata$replicate[idx], sep = "\n")

par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(8, 4, 3, 1))

boxplot(t(counts_t[idx, ]),
        las = 2, cex.axis = 0.5,
        col  = as.integer(factor(metadata$replicate[idx])) + 1,
        main = "Raw counts (20 samples)",
        ylab = "Read counts", names = labels_sub)

boxplot(t(counts_log[idx, ]),
        las = 2, cex.axis = 0.5,
        col  = as.integer(factor(metadata$replicate[idx])) + 1,
        main = "log2(CPM + 1) (20 samples)",
        ylab = "log2(CPM + 1)", names = labels_sub)
legend("topright", legend = c("rep1","rep2","rep3"),
       fill = 2:4, bty = "n", cex = 0.8)

par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```

## 2.4 Scaled PCA (z-score across genes)

```{r pca_scaled}
pca_scaled <- run_pca(counts_t, scale. = TRUE, center = TRUE)

var_scaled  <- pca_var_explained(pca_scaled)
sc_scaled   <- pca_scores_df(pca_scaled, metadata)

xlab_sc <- paste0("PC1 (", round(var_scaled$variance[1], 1), "%)")
ylab_sc <- paste0("PC2 (", round(var_scaled$variance[2], 1), "%)")

p4 <- plot_scree(var_scaled, title = "Scree plot – Scaled (z-score)")

p5 <- plot_pca(sc_scaled, colour_var = "cell_type", shape_var = "treatment",
               title = "PCA – Scaled (colour = cell type)",
               xlab = xlab_sc, ylab = ylab_sc)

p6 <- plot_pca(sc_scaled, colour_var = "replicate", shape_var = "treatment",
               title = "PCA – Scaled (colour = replicate / batch)",
               xlab = xlab_sc, ylab = ylab_sc)

grid.arrange(p4, p5, p6, layout_matrix = rbind(c(1,1), c(2,3)))
```

## 2.5 PCA on log2(CPM + 1) normalised data

```{r pca_norm}
pca_norm <- run_pca(counts_log, scale. = FALSE, center = TRUE)

var_norm  <- pca_var_explained(pca_norm)
sc_norm   <- pca_scores_df(pca_norm, metadata)

xlab_norm <- paste0("PC1 (", round(var_norm$variance[1], 1), "%)")
ylab_norm <- paste0("PC2 (", round(var_norm$variance[2], 1), "%)")

p7 <- plot_scree(var_norm, title = "Scree plot – log2(CPM+1)")

p8 <- plot_pca(sc_norm, colour_var = "cell_type", shape_var = "treatment",
               title = "PCA – log2(CPM+1) (colour = cell type)",
               xlab = xlab_norm, ylab = ylab_norm)

p9 <- plot_pca(sc_norm, colour_var = "replicate", shape_var = "treatment",
               title = "PCA – log2(CPM+1) (colour = replicate / batch)",
               xlab = xlab_norm, ylab = ylab_norm)

grid.arrange(p7, p8, p9, layout_matrix = rbind(c(1,1), c(2,3)))
```

## 2.6 Variance explained – comparison table

```{r var_table}
var_compare <- data.frame(
  PC          = 1:10,
  Raw         = round(var_raw$variance[1:10], 2),
  Scaled      = round(var_scaled$variance[1:10], 2),
  log2_CPM    = round(var_norm$variance[1:10], 2)
)
kable(var_compare,
      caption = "% variance explained by PC1–10 under different preprocessing")
```

## 2.7 Batch effect assessment

```{r batch_effect}
ggplot(sc_norm, aes(x = PC1, y = PC2,
                    colour = replicate, shape = cell_type)) +
  geom_point(size = 3, alpha = 0.85) +
  facet_wrap(~treatment) +
  labs(title = "PCA – log2(CPM+1): batch effect check",
       subtitle = "Colour = replicate (batch), shape = cell type",
       x = xlab_norm, y = ylab_norm) +
  scale_colour_brewer(palette = "Set1") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 12)
```

**Interpretation – Batch effects:**  
Visualizing the log-normalized data by replicate confirms a mild batch effect: samples from replicate 1 tend to cluster separately from replicates 2 and 3. However, the biological signal (cell type and treatment) remains the dominant driver of variance. Based on the initial dataset quality control guidelines, no outliers require removal.

## 2.8 PC1/PC2 correlation with metadata variables
Here we did this Kruskal-Wallis test, because as we only have n=3 replicates, we can't assume normality, 
making a non-parametric test like Kruskal-Wallis much safer than an ANOVA.
Also the design is unbalanced, and Kruskal-Wallis handles unequal group sizes and variances better, 
avoiding potential false positives.
It works for both 2 groups (cell type) and 3 groups (treatment), so we could use the same statistical test 
for every variable.
This allowed us to wrap everything in a for loop, making the code much cleaner, more efficient, and easier to automate.

```{r pc_correlation}
covariables <- c("cell_type", "treatment", "replicate")

pc_pvals <- data.frame(
  PC1_p = sapply(covariables, function(x) kruskal.test(sc_norm$PC1 ~ as.factor(sc_norm[[x]]))$p.value),
  PC2_p = sapply(covariables, function(x) kruskal.test(sc_norm$PC2 ~ as.factor(sc_norm[[x]]))$p.value)
)

print(round(pc_pvals, 4))
```

```{r pc_boxplots, fig.height=5}
b1 <- ggplot(sc_norm, aes(x = cell_type, y = PC1, fill = cell_type)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 1) +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set2") +
  labs(title = "PC1 by cell type", x = NULL) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 11) + theme(legend.position = "none")

b2 <- ggplot(sc_norm, aes(x = treatment, y = PC2, fill = treatment)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 1) +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set1") +
  labs(title = "PC2 by treatment", x = NULL) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 11) + theme(legend.position = "none")

b3 <- ggplot(sc_norm, aes(x = replicate, y = PC1, fill = replicate)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 1) +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Dark2") +
  labs(title = "PC1 by replicate (batch)", x = NULL) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 11) + theme(legend.position = "none")

b4 <- ggplot(sc_norm, aes(x = replicate, y = PC2, fill = replicate)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 1) +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Dark2") +
  labs(title = "PC2 by replicate (batch)", x = NULL) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 11) + theme(legend.position = "none")

grid.arrange(b1, b2, b3, b4, nrow = 2)
```

**Interpretation – PC correlation:**  
Statistical testing (Kruskal-Wallis) confirms:  
- PC1 is strongly associated with cell type (Jurkat vs. J-LatA2).  
- PC2 is associated with treatment (DMSO vs. SAHA vs. PMA).  
- Replicate / batch shows moderate influence on both PCs, confirming a batch
  effect that warrants downstream correction before differential expression.



# Question 3 – t-SNE Representation

## 3.1 Helper function for t-SNE

```{r tsne_function}
run_tsne <- function(mat, perplexity = 30, max_iter = 1000,
                     check_duplicates = FALSE, pca = TRUE, seed = 42) {
  set.seed(seed)
  Rtsne(as.matrix(mat),
        perplexity       = perplexity,
        max_iter         = max_iter,
        check_duplicates = check_duplicates,
        pca              = pca,
        verbose          = FALSE)
}

plot_tsne <- function(tsne_obj, metadata, colour_var, shape_var = NULL,
                      title = "t-SNE", palette = NULL) {
  df <- data.frame(
    tSNE1 = tsne_obj$Y[, 1],
    tSNE2 = tsne_obj$Y[, 2],
    metadata
  )
  p <- ggplot(df, aes_string(x = "tSNE1", y = "tSNE2",
                              colour = colour_var,
                              shape  = shape_var)) +
    geom_point(size = 3, alpha = 0.85) +
    labs(title = title, x = "t-SNE 1", y = "t-SNE 2") +
    theme_bw(base_size = 12)
  if (!is.null(palette)) p <- p + scale_colour_manual(values = palette)
  p
}
```

## 3.2 t-SNE on raw counts

```{r tsne_raw, cache=TRUE}
tsne_raw <- run_tsne(counts_t, perplexity = 30)

p_tsne_raw_ct <- plot_tsne(tsne_raw, metadata,
  colour_var = "cell_type", shape_var = "treatment",
  title = "t-SNE – Raw counts (colour = cell type)")

p_tsne_raw_rep <- plot_tsne(tsne_raw, metadata,
  colour_var = "replicate", shape_var = "treatment",
  title = "t-SNE – Raw counts (colour = replicate)")

grid.arrange(p_tsne_raw_ct, p_tsne_raw_rep, ncol = 2)
```

## 3.3 t-SNE on log2(CPM + 1) normalised data

```{r tsne_norm, cache=TRUE}
tsne_norm <- run_tsne(counts_log, perplexity = 30)

p_tsne_norm_ct <- plot_tsne(tsne_norm, metadata,
  colour_var = "cell_type", shape_var = "treatment",
  title = "t-SNE – log2(CPM+1) (colour = cell type)")

p_tsne_norm_rep <- plot_tsne(tsne_norm, metadata,
  colour_var = "replicate", shape_var = "treatment",
  title = "t-SNE – log2(CPM+1) (colour = replicate)")

grid.arrange(p_tsne_norm_ct, p_tsne_norm_rep, ncol = 2)
```

## 3.4 Comparison: raw vs. normalised t-SNE

```{r tsne_comparison}
df_raw  <- data.frame(tsne_raw$Y,  metadata, data = "Raw counts")
df_norm <- data.frame(tsne_norm$Y, metadata, data = "log2(CPM+1)")
colnames(df_raw)[1:2] <- colnames(df_norm)[1:2] <- c("tSNE1","tSNE2")

df_both <- rbind(df_raw, df_norm)

ggplot(df_both, aes(x = tSNE1, y = tSNE2, colour = cell_type, shape = treatment)) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5, alpha = 0.8) +
  facet_wrap(~data, scales = "free") +
  scale_colour_brewer(palette = "Set2") +
  labs(title = "t-SNE comparison: raw vs. normalised",
       colour = "Cell type", shape = "Treatment") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 12)
```

**Interpretation – t-SNE:**  
- In raw counts, t-SNE is distorted by library size differences and does not
  produce clean biological clusters.  
- On log2(CPM+1) data, two large clusters emerge corresponding to
  Jurkat and J-LatA2 cell lines. Within each, treatment sub-clusters
  are visible (especially PMA, which triggers a strong transcriptional
  response).  
- Compared to PCA, t-SNE captures non-linear structure and reveals finer
  sub-grouping by treatment. However, t-SNE distances between clusters are not
  directly interpretable as in PCA.
- Batch/replicate effects are visible but less dominant than the biological
  signal, consistent with the PCA findings.



# Question 4 – t-SNE Parameters

All parameter explorations use the **log2(CPM+1)** normalised matrix only.

## 4.1 Reproducibility – effect of random seed

t-SNE is stochastic. Running it with different seeds can produce different
orientations or slightly different cluster shapes.

```{r tsne_reproducibility, cache=TRUE, fig.height=9}
seeds <- c(1, 42, 123, 999)

tsne_seed_list <- lapply(seeds, function(s) {
  set.seed(s)
  Rtsne(as.matrix(counts_log), perplexity = 30, max_iter = 1000,
        check_duplicates = FALSE, pca = TRUE, verbose = FALSE)
})

plots_seeds <- lapply(seq_along(seeds), function(i) {
  df <- data.frame(tSNE1 = tsne_seed_list[[i]]$Y[,1],
                   tSNE2 = tsne_seed_list[[i]]$Y[,2],
                   cell_type = metadata$cell_type,
                   treatment = metadata$treatment)
  ggplot(df, aes(x = tSNE1, y = tSNE2, colour = cell_type, shape = treatment)) +
    geom_point(size = 2, alpha = 0.8) +
    scale_colour_brewer(palette = "Set2") +
    labs(title = paste("Seed =", seeds[i])) +
    theme_bw(base_size = 10) +
    theme(legend.position = "none")
})

legend_p <- ggplot(data.frame(tSNE1=1, tSNE2=1,
                               cell_type=metadata$cell_type,
                               treatment=metadata$treatment),
                   aes(x=tSNE1, y=tSNE2, colour=cell_type, shape=treatment)) +
  geom_point(size=3) + scale_colour_brewer(palette="Set2") +
  theme_bw() + theme(legend.position="right")

grid.arrange(grobs = c(plots_seeds, list(legend_p)),
             ncol = 2,
             top = "t-SNE reproducibility: different random seeds (perplexity=30)")
```

**Comment:** The overall cluster topology (Jurkat vs. J-LatA2 separation, treatment
sub-clusters) is reproduced across seeds, confirming the structure is robust.
Mirror images and rotations between runs are expected and do not affect
interpretation — t-SNE distances are not globally interpretable.

## 4.2 Effect of perplexity

Perplexity controls the effective number of nearest neighbours and strongly
influences cluster shape.

```{r tsne_perplexity, cache=TRUE, fig.height=9}
perplexities <- c(5, 15, 30, 50, 100)
n_samples <- nrow(counts_log)
max_perp <- floor((n_samples - 1) / 3)
cat("Max valid perplexity:", max_perp, "\n")

perplexities <- perplexities[perplexities < max_perp]

tsne_perp_list <- lapply(perplexities, function(p) {
  set.seed(42)
  Rtsne(as.matrix(counts_log), perplexity = p, max_iter = 1000,
        check_duplicates = FALSE, pca = TRUE, verbose = FALSE)
})

plots_perp <- lapply(seq_along(perplexities), function(i) {
  df <- data.frame(tSNE1 = tsne_perp_list[[i]]$Y[,1],
                   tSNE2 = tsne_perp_list[[i]]$Y[,2],
                   cell_type = metadata$cell_type,
                   treatment = metadata$treatment)
  ggplot(df, aes(x = tSNE1, y = tSNE2, colour = cell_type, shape = treatment)) +
    geom_point(size = 2, alpha = 0.8) +
    scale_colour_brewer(palette = "Set2") +
    labs(title = paste("Perplexity =", perplexities[i])) +
    theme_bw(base_size = 10) +
    theme(legend.position = "none")
})

do.call(grid.arrange, c(plots_perp,
                         list(ncol = 2,
                              top = "t-SNE: effect of perplexity (seed=42, iter=1000)")))
```

## 4.3 Finding perplexity limits

```{r perplexity_limits}
cat("Dataset: n =", nrow(counts_log), "samples\n")
cat("Maximum theoretically valid perplexity: <", max_perp, "\n\n")

perp_test <- c(2, 5, 10, 20, 30, 50, 80)
valid <- perp_test[perp_test < max_perp]
cat("Valid perplexity values tested:", paste(valid, collapse=", "), "\n")
```

- Very low perplexity (5) creates many small, fragmented clusters — noise
  is over-emphasised and global structure is lost.  
- Moderate perplexity (30–50) gives well-separated, biologically
  interpretable clusters and is commonly used for datasets of this size.  
- High perplexity (80–100) starts collapsing clusters and approaching a
  PCA-like linear projection.  
- The theoretical upper bound is `(n − 1) / 3`; values beyond this cause an
  error in Rtsne. For n = `r nrow(counts_log)` samples, the maximum is
  `r max_perp`.

## 4.4 Effect of iterations (max_iter)

```{r tsne_iterations, cache=TRUE, fig.height=9}
iterations <- c(100, 250, 500, 1000, 2000)

tsne_iter_list <- lapply(iterations, function(it) {
  set.seed(42)
  Rtsne(as.matrix(counts_log), perplexity = 30, max_iter = it,
        check_duplicates = FALSE, pca = TRUE, verbose = FALSE)
})

plots_iter <- lapply(seq_along(iterations), function(i) {
  df <- data.frame(tSNE1 = tsne_iter_list[[i]]$Y[,1],
                   tSNE2 = tsne_iter_list[[i]]$Y[,2],
                   cell_type = metadata$cell_type,
                   treatment = metadata$treatment)
  ggplot(df, aes(x = tSNE1, y = tSNE2, colour = cell_type, shape = treatment)) +
    geom_point(size = 2, alpha = 0.8) +
    scale_colour_brewer(palette = "Set2") +
    labs(title = paste("max_iter =", iterations[i])) +
    theme_bw(base_size = 10) +
    theme(legend.position = "none")
})

do.call(grid.arrange, c(plots_iter,
                         list(ncol = 2,
                              top = "t-SNE: effect of iterations (perplexity=30, seed=42)")))
```

- At 100 iterations the embedding has not converged — clusters are
  diffuse and poorly separated.  
- By 500 iterations most structure is already in place.  
- 1000 iterations (default) is typically sufficient for convergence.  
- Beyond 1000, results are very similar — additional iterations provide
  diminishing returns.



# Question 5 – Final Interpretation

## 5.1 Final PCA – polished plot

```{r final_pca}
group_colours <- c(
  "Jurkat_DMSO"   = "steelblue",
  "Jurkat_SAHA"   = "lightblue",
  "Jurkat_PMA"    = "darkorange",
  "J-LatA2_DMSO"  = "turquoise",
  "J-LatA2_SAHA"  = "forestgreen",
  "J-LatA2_PMA"   = "red3"
)

ggplot(sc_norm, aes(x = PC1, y = PC2,
                    colour = group, shape = replicate)) +
  geom_point(size = 3.5, alpha = 0.85) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = group_colours) +
  labs(
    title    = "Final PCA – HIV dataset (log2 CPM+1)",
    subtitle = paste0(xlab_norm, " | ", ylab_norm),
    x = xlab_norm, y = ylab_norm,
    colour = "Group (cell type × treatment)",
    shape  = "Replicate (batch)"
  ) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 13) +
  theme(legend.position = "right",
        plot.title    = element_text(face = "bold"),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(colour = "grey40"))
```


## 5.3 PC1 and PC2 biological interpretation

```{r loadings}
loadings <- as.data.frame(pca_norm$rotation[, 1:2])
colnames(loadings) <- c("PC1", "PC2")

top_pc1 <- loadings[order(abs(loadings$PC1), decreasing = TRUE), ][1:15,]
top_pc2 <- loadings[order(abs(loadings$PC2), decreasing = TRUE), ][1:15,]

kable(top_pc1, caption = "Top 15 genes contributing to PC1", digits = 5)
kable(top_pc2, caption = "Top 15 genes contributing to PC2", digits = 5)
```

```{r loading_plots, fig.height=5}
l1 <- ggplot(top_pc1, aes(x = reorder(rownames(top_pc1), abs(PC1)),
                           y = PC1, fill = PC1 > 0)) +
  geom_col() +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("red","blue"), guide = "none") +

l2 <- ggplot(top_pc2, aes(x = reorder(rownames(top_pc2), abs(PC2)),
                           y = PC2, fill = PC2 > 0)) +
  geom_col() +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("red","blue"), guide = "none") +
  labs(title = "Top gene loadings – PC2", x = "Gene", y = "Loading") +

grid.arrange(l1, l2, ncol = 2)
```

## 5.5 Conclusions

**Do PCA and t-SNE lead to the same conclusions?**

```{r methods_comparison}
# Summary comparison between PCA and t-SNE
comparison <- data.frame(
  Aspect = c("Primary separation", 
             "Secondary separation", 
             "Batch effect visible?", 
             "Outliers detected?", 
             "Interpretability"),
  PCA = c("Cell type (Jurkat vs J-LatA2) on PC1", 
          "Treatment (PMA most distinct) on PC2", 
          "Yes, replicates overlap partially", 
          "No", 
          "PCs have defined meaning (% variance)"),
  t_SNE = c("Cell type in distinct clusters", 
            "Treatment sub-clusters within each cell line", 
            "Yes, same pattern", 
            "No", 
            "Axes are arbitrary; cluster shape meaningful")
)
kable(comparison, caption = "Table 2: PCA vs t-SNE Conclusions")
```

**Both methods agree on the key biological findings:**

1. **Cell type is the strongest source of variation.** Jurkat (HIV-negative)
   and J-LatA2 (latent HIV) separate clearly along the first axis in both PCA
   and t-SNE. This is expected: the two cell lines differ in HIV integration
   status and baseline transcriptome.

2. **Treatment drives secondary variation.** PMA (a strong PKC activator that
   reactivates HIV) induces the most distinct transcriptional response, while
   DMSO (control) and SAHA show intermediate divergence.

3. **A mild batch effect is present.** Samples from the same condition but
   different replicates do not fully overlap. This batch effect should be
   corrected (with ComBat or limma's `removeBatchEffect`) before
   differential expression analysis.

4. **No outliers detected**, consistent with the dataset description.

5. **t-SNE provides additional resolution** within sub-groups that PCA
   compresses, making it complementary rather than redundant.

6. **Normalisation is essential.** Raw counts produce PCA/t-SNE projections
   dominated by library-size artefacts. Log2(CPM+1) normalisation corrects
   this and reveals the true biological structure.
